changelog: Insert a new core principle warning that very short trailing fragments (≤3 words or bare name/location/measure/preposition) can, taken alone, assert/negate or remap scope and so should be treated as high contra-risk and ranked low — directly addresses the primary_finding about underestimated entailment risk for short fragments.

Replace C2 to add a concise rule that explicitly flags very short trailing fragments and bare names/places/measures as high entailment (contra) risk, addressing the primary finding without duplicating the sibling insertion.

Replace E1 (hand-written example) with measured labeled example en_us_1567 so the scorer sees a real failure case where a very short trailing fragment (≤3 words) causes high entailment (contra) risk, addressing the primary finding.

Replace C3 to keep the subordinator/attachment warning but add a concise rule flagging very short trailing fragments (≤3 words or bare name/place/measure/preposition) as high entailment (contra) risk — directly addresses the primary finding with a single small change distinct from sibling edits.
